events.text: The Rock Crystal egg was created in 1896 for Empress Alexandra Feodorovna.
events.subject: self
events.quote: It was created in 1896 for Empress Alexandra Feodorovna .

events.text: The egg was created by workmaster Mikhail Evlampievich Perkhin.
events.subject: self
events.quote: The egg was created by Faberges workmaster , Mikhail Evlampievich Perkhin

events.text: Nicholas and Alexandra had just been married two years prior, in 1894.
events.subject: other
events.quote: as they had just been married two years prior , in 1894

events.text: Nicholas and Alexandra were engaged to be married at Veste Coburg during the wedding of Alexandra's brother Ernie in 1894.
events.subject: self
events.quote: The palace where Nicholas and Alexandra were engaged to be married , during the wedding of Alexandras brother Ernie

events.text: Nicholas II presented the egg to Alexandra Fedorovna.
events.subject: self
events.quote: The egg was presented by Nicholas II to Alexandra Fedorovna on March 24 , 1896 .

events.text: The egg was housed in the Empress study in the Winter Palace.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1909 , the egg was housed in the Empress study in the Winter Palace .

events.text: The egg was seized by the Kerensky Provisional Government and moved to the Armory Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow.
events.subject: self
events.quote: The egg was seized by the Kerensky Provisional Government and moved to the Armory Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow

events.text: The Rock Crystal Egg was one of the ten Eggs sold by the Antikvariat to the Hammer Galleries in New York City.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1930 , the Rock Crystal Egg was one of the ten Eggs sold by the Antikvariat ( Trade Department ) to the Hammer Galleries in New York City

events.text: The egg became the last of five Imperial Easter Eggs bought by Lillian Thomas Pratt.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1945 the egg became the last of five Imperial Easter Eggs bought by Lillian Thomas Pratt

events.text: Upon Lillian Thomas Pratt's death, the egg was willed to Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, Richmond, Virginia.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Upon Lillian Thomas Pratts death in 1947 , the egg was willed to Virginia Museum of Fine Arts , Richmond , Virginia .
